records.finding: The log SDK batch queue (2048) overwrites its oldest record on overflow and reports it through no channel the caller can reach, while emit's event buffer is 10,000 and Flush passes one batch. Outcome events were destroyed silently while every layer reported success.
records.evidence: sdk/log@v0.22.0 batch.go: dfltMaxQSize=2048; Enqueue advances read and bumps a dropped counter only global.Warn'd; OnEmit returns nil unconditionally; Logger.Emit routes errors to otel.Handle. emit/emitter.go: bufSize 10000, Flush passes s.events in one ExportEvents call.
records.reason: Queue sized explicitly and emit chunked to it, flushing each chunk. Mutation-proven: restoring the default queue and unchunked emit delivers 6691-8925 of 10000 across runs. The first regression test was worthless — against an instant exporter the processor drains as fast as a caller fills it — so the fixture now models a slow collector, which is the incident condition.

records.finding: Anything outside a two-entry gauge map fell through a bare else to a monotonic delta Sum, so a typo'd or future level family shipped as a counter and would be summed by the backend.
records.evidence: metrics.go gaugeFamilies had two entries and an else branch; prometheus.go:188, cloudwatch/emf.go:44, gcp/monitoring.go all reject an unrecognised family with an error.
records.reason: Explicit known-family set (the ADR-0004 five plus ADR-0012's gauge) and an unknownFamilyError returned before anything reaches the backend. Round 3 verified the set matches the three siblings family-for-family and that nothing legitimate is rejected.

records.finding: The conformance harness replaced the whole eventSink, excising buildRecord, the LoggerProvider, the BatchProcessor and ForceFlush, so 'events flush on shutdown with no loss' counted acceptance and could not fail.
records.evidence: countingEvents implemented eventSink with c.events += len(batch). cloudwatch cuts at the io.Writer and gcp at the http Doer, both leaving the real pipeline intact.
records.reason: Seam moved to a fake sdklog.Exporter behind the real provider and batch processor. Round 3 confirmed the real pipeline now runs and that countingMetric remains a legitimate seam because buildResourceMetrics still executes.

records.finding: providerSink.emit and New ran only under a //go:build integration tag that self-skips without a live collector, so the trace-link branch, the malformed-hex fallthrough and the FlagsSampled forcing were pinned by nothing.
records.evidence: integration_test.go:1 build tag plus a t.Skip on OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; no other test referenced providerSink or New.
records.reason: Unit-tested over an in-memory exporter across empty, valid, malformed, wrong-length and all-zero trace ids. Round 3 micro-mutated both branches and confirmed the tests kill each.

records.finding: ResourceMetrics.Resource was never set, so with no writer identity in the ADR-0004 label sets N replicas shared one gauge series and the deferred leg under-reported by roughly N.
records.evidence: The composite literal set only ScopeMetrics. gcp/monitoring.go fixed the identical defect one commit earlier with a generic_task per-process task_id.
records.reason: Default resource carries service.name and a per-process service.instance.id, overridable with WithResource. Round 2 then found it reached only the metric leg; see the following finding.

records.finding: Present-tense claim that a query adapter parses this record shape when no GCP/OTLP query adapter exists.
records.evidence: adapters/query holds only cwinsights, promql and sql.
records.reason: Reworded to state the EMF mirroring as fact. (Carried from the sibling GCP branch's wording.)

records.finding: 'an exporter that does not recognise a family fails loudly (a conformance test pins this)' — the first half became false when this diff added the OTLP row; the second half was never true.
records.evidence: testkit/conformance Check() emits only declares-a-signal, no-loss, capability-honesty and empty-noop invariants; git log -S finds no family-recognition case ever.
records.reason: First half made true by the family-rejection fix; the sentence now says where the property is actually pinned (per-adapter unit tests). The never-true clause predates this branch and is corrected rather than inherited.

records.finding: The new prose recommended OTLP for Google Cloud 'rather than reaching for a cloud-specific client' three lines below the GCP adapter's own supported row and its twelve-line footnote, and README made the claim inside the paragraph selling dependency leanness.
records.evidence: docs/adapters.md listed adapters/export/gcp as supported with a footnote teaching correct use; gcp's module pulls nothing beyond stdlib while otlp pulls the otel module graph.
records.reason: Both restated as an explicit trade rather than a recommendation against a shipped adapter. Judged on the tree as it is: the item that removes the GCP metrics half has not landed.

records.finding: Package doc said 'gauge for biz_inflight_value' where the code has two gauge families, and opened 'the default shortfall exporter' when emit.New requires an explicit exporter.
records.evidence: metrics.go gaugeFamilies has two entries; emit/emitter.go New errors on a nil exporter.
records.reason: Both corrected.

records.finding: Candidate: conformance.go and emit/example_test.go comments still describe the two-collector world PR #79 edited them into.
records.evidence: PR #79 rewrote both parentheticals to drop OTLP mentions.
records.reason: REFUTED by the cross-examiner. Both are illustrative parentheticals attached to a general statement, not exhaustiveness claims, and the staleness predates this branch — the GCP adapter added a third conformance harness one commit earlier without updating them either. Editing them would assert an exhaustiveness the sentences never claimed.

records.finding: Round 1's own fix was incomplete: the chunking guarantee was per-call, not per-queue. Overlapping ExportEvents calls share one queue and still overflowed it.
records.evidence: providerSink.emit held no lock; measured 4848-5533 of 8192 outcomes destroyed with no error returned. emit.Std.Flush releases s.mu before calling the exporter and its ticker can race a caller-driven Flush, so the overlap is reachable through emit's own API.
records.reason: A mutex across providerSink.emit. Mutation-proven at 5095/8192 with the lock deleted. Round 3 verified the lock covers every ForceFlush, that no other path reaches the queue, and that it introduces no deadlock or unbounded stall.

records.finding: The default resource reached only the metric leg; the log provider was built without sdklog.WithResource and fell back to the SDK default, so metrics and events disagreed about who wrote them.
records.evidence: Events carried service.name=unknown_service:<binary> with no instance id while metrics carried the real identity; WithResource's doc claimed it governed 'every exported point'.
records.reason: Resource threads into newProviderSink on both construction paths. Mutation-proven: dropping WithResource fails the parity test with service.name=unknown_service:otlp.test.

records.finding: Two of four subtests were named as overflow coverage they cannot provide: the processor drains 512 records per export, so a 2049-record batch never fills a 2048-entry queue.
records.evidence: Under the unchunked mutation only the 10000 case fails; the 2048 and 2049 cases pass.
records.reason: Renamed to the chunk arithmetic they actually pin, with the test comment naming which case carries the regression. Round 3 re-ran the mutation and confirmed the names are now exactly accurate.

records.finding: New comments used ALL-CAPS emphasis, narrated change history and argued with the reviewer, against ADR-0014's Comments section.
records.evidence: ADR-0014 forbids ALL-CAPS emphasis, change history and reviewer persuasion ('deliberately').
records.reason: Rewritten. Round 3 found the sweep incomplete AND that the round-2 fix reintroduced 'deliberately' inside the very comment it rewrote; all three survivors are now gone, verified by grepping every added comment line across the branch.

records.finding: 'OTLP hands aggregation to the SDK' is false — this adapter builds metricdata by hand and has no MeterProvider, Reader or View anywhere.
records.evidence: grep for MeterProvider/accumulat/cumulative over the module's non-test sources returns nothing.
records.reason: Restated to the true and stronger claim: it has no in-process accumulator at all, because emit produces deltas and OTLP takes delta temporality.

records.finding: 'pulling the gRPC stack into that module' read as a transport claim; the adapter speaks OTLP over HTTP and grpc/protobuf are indirect module-graph deps.
records.evidence: Only otlploghttp and otlpmetrichttp are imported; go.mod marks grpc and protobuf // indirect.
records.reason: Restated as indirect dependencies on the HTTP transport. Round 3 noted the doc if anything understates it: 66 grpc and 36 protobuf packages are in the non-test import closure.

records.finding: The eventQueueSize comment said it was 'the chunk size emit ships in' — emit is an imported package here and does no chunking; and providerSink.queueSize was dead indirection whose zero value made the chunk loop spin forever.
records.evidence: providerSink.emit does the chunking; queueSize was written once from the constant and never varied.
records.reason: Comment corrected and extended with why the constant is not tied to emit's buffer and that setting it overrides OTEL_BLRP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE; the field removed in favour of the constant. Round 3 verified every claim in the new comment against the pinned SDK source.

records.finding: Round 3 verdicted round 2's comment-hygiene finding NOT addressed: three ADR-0014 violations survived, one of them introduced by the round-2 fix inside the comment it rewrote to satisfy that finding.
records.evidence: 'deliberately not tied to emit's larger event buffer' (new in the fix commit), 'The sampled flag is set deliberately', and ALL-CAPS 'the SAME gauge series'.
records.reason: All three removed and re-grepped across every comment line added on the branch.

records.finding: providerSink.mu's doc used 'emit' for two different things — the method it annotates and the imported package — so read the obvious way it said this method does not hold its lock across the exporter call, the opposite of what it does.
records.evidence: providerSink.emit holds s.mu across every ForceFlush; the intended referent was emit.Std.Flush, which releases its own lock before calling the exporter.
records.reason: Names emit.Std.Flush explicitly.

records.finding: Self-caught at rebase: the C4 level-2 diagram landed on main while this branch was open and enumerates the export adapters, so adding one without updating it would leave a diagram on the old adapter set.
records.evidence: The export band read 'prometheus · cloudwatch EMF · gcp'. ADR-0008 names diagrams explicitly among the artifacts a contract change may not leave describing old behaviour.
records.reason: Band now names otlp. Found by rebasing onto current main rather than by review — the enumeration did not exist when this branch started.

records.finding: The two overflow regression tests discriminate only when the producer outruns the exporter's drain, which the race detector prevents: under -race the concurrency test passes 13/13 with the serialising lock deleted.
records.evidence: Without -race the same mutant fails 12/12 (5120-7657 of 8192) and still fails at GOMAXPROCS=1 and 2. scripts/ci-go.sh runs plain go test, so the protection is real as shipped.
records.reason: PARKED as workspace-yqu, not dismissed on the merits, and adjudicated at the repair cap. The regression protection is genuine in the configuration CI actually runs. The exposure is latent: adding -race to the core job would silently retire both tests. The bead carries the fix (have the fixture create the overflow window explicitly) and the related weakness that the writer-identity test asserts two literals rather than comparing the legs. The commit-message correction — that 'go test -race green' was evidence gathered where the test cannot fail — is recorded on the branch.

records.finding: Shutdown is terminal for the event leg where all three siblings' Shutdown is not, and a post-Shutdown emit returns nil having delivered nothing while the metric leg on the same object returns a loud error.
records.evidence: sdklog OnEmit returns immediately once stopped and ForceFlush returns nil; cloudwatch, prometheus and gcp all keep working after Shutdown; otlpmetrichttp returns errShutdown.
records.reason: PARKED as workspace-9h1. Not reachable through emit.Std's own lifecycle — Close is sync.Once-guarded and orders Flush, Flush, Shutdown — so it needs a caller invoking Flush after Close. The bead also asks which answer is the repo-wide contract, since four adapters currently implement three.

records.finding: sdklog.WithResource merges resource.Environment() and the metric path assigns verbatim, so OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES reaches events only, while WithResource's doc claims it governs both signals.
records.evidence: Probe with OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES set: the log record carried deployment.environment and k8s.pod.name; the metric resource did not. Identity attributes still agree because the explicit resource wins the merge.
records.reason: PARKED as workspace-a9f. The writer-identity guarantee this branch delivers is intact; this is a separate, smaller divergence, and the module points users at the standard OTel environment so it is worth closing.

records.finding: The mutex acquisition is not context-aware, so ExportEvents can block past its own ctx deadline waiting for another caller's in-flight flush.
records.evidence: s.mu.Lock() ignores ctx; the wait is bounded by the other caller's remaining chunks times the SDK's 30s export timeout.
records.reason: RULED ON at the repair cap rather than parked. The reviewer established this is not on the request path: emit.Std.Record never touches ExportEvents — it appends to a bounded buffer and returns — and ExportEvents is reached only from Flush, called by the background ticker or an explicit caller. So serialising cannot block a payments request. The only observable effect is that a caller-driven Flush queues behind the ticker's flush instead of interleaving with it, which is precisely the interleaving that caused the data loss. The residue is that Close(ctx) with a short deadline can overrun it while waiting; that is a worse outcome than losing money events, which is what the lock prevents.

records.finding: CI's core job failed on staticcheck SA1019 after local verify and gate parity were both green: attribute.Value.Emit is deprecated in favour of Value.String.
records.evidence: repo.yaml verify.core runs fmt, vet, build, test; .github/workflows/ci.yml's core job runs those plus vuln and lint. go vet does not do deprecation analysis, and golangci-lint is not installed in this environment, so no local step could have surfaced it.
records.reason: Both call sites use Value.String, which is the documented replacement with identical behaviour for these assertions. The underlying parity gap is filed as workspace-dfd — repo.yaml, .github/ and scripts/ are gate surface, changeable only in a PR whose tracked item is explicitly about CI, which this bead is not.
